==English== {{wp|}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*steh₂-}} {{etymon|en|id=polity|:inh|enm:stat|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|stat}} (as a noun); adopted c. 1200 from both {{der|en|fro|estat}} and {{der|en|la|stātus||manner of standing, attitude, position, carriage, manner, dress, apparel; and other senses}}, from {{m|la|stō|stāre|to stand}}. {{doublet|en|estate|status}}. The sense of "polity" develops in the 14th century. Compare {{cog|fr|être}}, {{cog|el|στέω}}, {{cog|it|stare}}, {{cog|pt|estar}}, {{cog|ro|sta}}, and {{cog|es|estar}}. The verb is first attested around the beginning of the 16th century. Related to {{cog|en|stand}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|hād||state, condition}} and {{noncog|ang|cynewīse||state, nation}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/steɪt/|a=RP,GA}} * {{audio|en|En-uk-state.ogg|a=RP}} * {{audio|en|En-us-state.ogg|a=GA}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪt|s=1}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun|~}} # {{senseid|en|condition}} A [[condition]]; a [[set]] of [[circumstance]]s applying at any given [[time]]. #: {{uxi|en|a '''state''' of being}} #: {{uxi|en|a '''state''' of emergency}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1697|tlr=w:John Dryden|chapter=[[w:Aenid|Æneis]]|title=The Works of {{w|Virgil}}|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QzIJAAAAQAAJ|volume=III|location=Londo|publisher=w:Jacob Tonson|year_published=1721|page=713|passage=Relate what ''Latium'' was, her ancient Kings : / Declare the paſt, and preſent '''State''' of things, / When firſt the ''Trojan'' Fleet ''Auſonia'' ſought ; / And how the Rivals lov’d, and how they fought.}} #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=I corralled the judge, and we started off across the fields, in no very mild '''state''' of fear of that gentleman's wife, whose vigilance was seldom relaxed.}} ## {{lb|en|physics}} A [[complete]] [[description]] of a [[system]], consisting of [[parameter]]s that determine all [[property|properties]] of the system. ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1977|author=J. It is used to communicate an absence of reasonable doubt and to emphasize the factual or truthful nature of the communication. The poet and journalist William Cullen Bryant listed ''state'', when used as a synonym for ''say'', in his style guide for ''The New York Evening Post'', which he called the "Index Expurgatorius".
